transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. At 12 years old, a 'rough rattly growl' combined with weak suction usually points to one of two things: a significant internal blockage choking the airflow, or worn motor bearings causing noise and loss of power. The next most likely cause is a physical obstruction in the airway that isn't immediately visible. Please detach the hose from both ends (machine body and wand/floorhead) and look through each section to ensure there is no blockage inside them. Did you find any blockages that needed clearing?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
Yes, I've done that. The hose is clear, a coin dropped straight through it. The suction is weak at both the hose end and at the head, so I don't think it's a blockage.

Since the airflow path is clear and filters are new, that 'rough rattly growl' combined with weak suction at 12 years old suggests worn motor bearings. The motor shaft wobbles, reducing efficiency (weak suction) and creating that specific noise. To confirm this, we need to check the motor itself. If they feel gritty, stiff, or scrape against the housing, the bearings are likely shot. Let me know what you find.

I'm afraid I'm not confident taking the motor out, and I only have a screwdriver. Is there anything simpler I can check from the outside? I should also say that there is a hot, burning electrical smell after about five minutes of running.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Please do not use the vacuum again. The combination of a rough rattling noise and a burning electrical smell after just five minutes indicates that the motor is failing—likely due to worn bearings or an internal electrical short—which creates a genuine fire hazard. Because this involves the internal motor components and mains electricity, it cannot be safely repaired by a homeowner with only basic tools. Given the age of the machine (12 years) and the severity of these symptoms, it is not worth attempting a repair; you should arrange for professional disposal or recycling.
